title: Serino 2007 · Sighted cohort cane training
citation: Serino, A., Bassolino, M., Farnè, A., & Làdavas, E. (2007). Extended Multisensory Space in Blind Cane Users. Psychological Science, 18(7), 642–648.
notes: Published study settings are available for inspection. See the source-backed method and remaining execution requirements.

published_method.cohort: 16 right-handed sighted adults with normal or corrected vision, blindfolded during testing and training.
published_method.assessment_sequence: Counterbalance pre-training blocks for a 125 cm cane and a load-matched 14 cm handle. Repeat the cane condition immediately after training and one day later, with no intervening cane use.
published_method.intervention: Spend 10 minutes using the cane to locate objects on the floor, 50–150 cm ahead and up to 80 cm laterally on either side.
published_method.sound: A 150 ms white-noise burst comes from near the right hand or from the floor near the cane tip, approximately 125 cm from the hand. The loudspeakers are matched at the ears to 70 dB.
published_method.touch: Two pairs of electrodes on the dorsal right index finger, with weak/strong electrode nesting counterbalanced. Titrate the weak target to about 90% perceptibility and the strong nontarget to 100%.
published_method.response: Give a speeded vocal response to the weak target. Withhold for strong stimulation and sound-only catches.
published_method.trial_pool: The described 150-trial task has 30 rows for each near/far by weak/strong cell and 30 auditory-only catches. Thirty practice trials precede assessment. The publication does not state a grand total for the four assessment conditions.

source_provenance.value: Two identical loudspeakers. Computer recordings of both outputs compared spectrally.
source_provenance.gap: Original noise file, seed, sample rate and filter settings unavailable.

electrodes.routing: one pair weak, one pair strong
electrodes.placement: Weak pair between strong electrodes in half the participants. Reverse nesting in the other half.

The four paired families and the auditory-only catch family exhaust the reported trial pool.

baseline_count.gap: The reported trial families account for all 150 trials.

catch_count.gap: The article lists 30 of 150. Catch allocation by speaker and catch ordering unreported.
